intro.title: Base URL
intro.html: Every JSON endpoint is served under /api (for example /api/ping). The panel, the payload, the callback collector and the public share/beacon endpoints live OUTSIDE /api and are documented in the Public surface section below.

intro.title: Response envelope
intro.html:
Every /api response is the same JSON envelope. success is a boolean, data carries the payload (or null on error), error is a human-readable message (or null on success) and meta is an object that carries pagination for list endpoints.

{
  "success": true,
  "data": { },
  "error": null,
  "meta": { "pagination": { "total": 0, "page": 1, "per_page": 25, "pages": 0 } }
}

On failure the HTTP status matches the error (401 unauthenticated, 403 forbidden, 404 not found, 405 wrong method, 409 conflict, 422 validation, 429 rate-limited, 503 database unavailable).

intro.title: Authentication
intro.html:
Authenticated endpoints expect a bearer token in the Authorization: Bearer <token> header. Two token types, both validated by the same middleware:

  • Session tokens - issued by POST /api/auth/login. Default lifetime 7 days (SESSION_TTL). The panel stores it in sessionStorage.
  • API keys - long-lived (or TTL-bounded) tokens for use outside the panel, managed under /api/apikeys. The raw key is shown once at creation and never again.

Tokens are hashed at rest (SHA-256); the password hash and the 2FA secret are never returned by any endpoint. If an account has TOTP 2FA enabled, login returns a one-time challenge instead of a token and is completed via POST /api/auth/twofa (see Session & 2FA).

intro.title: Capabilities, CORS & rate limiting
intro.html:
Each endpoint requires specific capabilities, resolved from the user's role (admin, user, or custom) plus optional per-user overrides. The Cap: column in the tables below shows which. Owners always have full control over their own resources; *.viewall holders and admins bypass scoping. Advanced payload behaviours (persistent, spider, beacon, custom JS, pages, filters, extensions) need both the global switch in Settings and the owner's payload.behaviour capability.

CORS: panel/API endpoints answer only for the configured panel origin(s); the public surface (payload, callback, shared, beacon) is open. Rate limiting applies to login and registration (HTTP 429).

groups.title: Session & 2FA
groups.note: Login is open; the rest answer CORS for the panel origin.

rows.d: Verify credentials. Returns a session token, or { twofa_required, challenge, expires_in } when 2FA is on and no code was supplied. Rate-limited per IP and per username.
Complete a pending 2FA login challenge and receive the session token. Rate-limited per challenge and per IP.
Revoke the current bearer token.
Two-step TOTP enable. Step 1 (no body) returns { secret, otpauth_uri }; step 2 confirms a code against that secret and persists it.
Disable 2FA. Requires a valid current TOTP code OR the account password.

groups.title: Account & API keys
groups.note: User rows are always returned through the safe-field filter. API key management requires the apikey.manage capability.

rows.d: The current user (safe fields), the token type used, and the effective capability map.
GET reads the user's notepad text; POST saves it.
List the current user's API keys (id/name/last_used/created only - never the raw key or hash).
Create a named API key. Returns the raw token ONCE (201). ttl is optional expiry in seconds (0/absent = no expiry).
Revoke one of the current user's API keys.

groups.title: Users & Roles
groups.note: User management requires user.manage; creating/editing roles and setting per-user permission overrides require user.roles. You can only grant capabilities you hold, and only manage a user whose capabilities are a subset of your own. Self-service cannot change the caller's own role/capabilities.

rows.d: List all users (safe fields).
Create a user (201). role = any existing role (admin, user, or a custom role). Reuses the installer username/password rules.
One user (safe fields) plus the effective capability map.

rows.a: Cap: user.manage (user.roles for permissions), or self
rows.d: Manager: change role/username, reset password, or ban - only for a user whose capabilities are a subset of yours; changing permissions needs user.roles. Self: change own password (requires current_password); cannot change own role/caps.
Delete a user (revokes their tokens + sharing rows). Refuses deleting yourself or the last admin.
List all roles and their capability sets.
Create a role (name in body) or update an existing one (name in path). Can only grant capabilities the caller holds.
Delete a custom role. Built-in roles (admin, user) cannot be deleted.

groups.title: Registration
groups.note: Public self-registration, only available when signup_enabled is on.

rows.d: Create a new user account (201). When signup_mode is 'code', a valid signup code is required. Rate-limited per IP.

groups.title: Sharing (per-resource access)
groups.note: Table-driven over user_access; {table} is restricted to payloads|reports. Owner-or-admin only.

rows.d: List who has access to the resource plus the global-access flag.
action = add_user | remove_user | change_access (access_type view|edit) | make_global | remove_global. Returns the recomputed share state.

groups.title: Payloads
groups.note: Access = ownership or a user_access grant; admins see all. Create needs payload.create; advanced behaviours apply only when the global switch and the owner's behaviour capability both allow them (enforced server-side).

rows.d: List payloads the user owns or has shared access to (admins: all).
Create a payload owned by the caller (201). Validates the domain/identifier (no scheme, no trailing slash).
Full assembled config for one payload.

rows.params: { collect?, customjs?, customjs2?, extensions?, persistent?, spider?, beacon? }
rows.d: Update editable config. collect toggles honour the global collect_* switches; persistent/spider/beacon are rejected (422) when globally disabled.
Delete a payload (cascades pages/filters/collect/sharing; reports are kept and fall under the catch-all).
Add an extract page (201). path must start with / and not contain ~.
Remove a page from the payload.
Add an allow/deny domain filter (201). Validates the wildcard-domain format.
Remove a filter from the payload.
Reassign a payload to another owner (by username or id).

groups.title: Reports
groups.note: Reading needs report.view (+ view access for non-admins); archive/delete need edit access; shares need report.share + edit access. Shares are on-request only.

rows.params: query: page, per_page, search, payload, archive
rows.d: Paginated, searchable list. Non-admins are scoped to reports they may view; admins see all. payload=__catchall__ (admin) lists reports coupled to no payload; its total is capped (meta.capped). Pagination in meta.
Full report detail. The DOM is omitted inline when it exceeds dom_threshold - fetch it from the dom route instead.
Download the full captured DOM as a text/plain attachment.
Toggle the report's archive flag.
Delete the report plus its data, shares and screenshot file.
Create an on-request share (201) exposing only the selected shareable columns. Returns the slug + public /s/{slug} URL.
List a report's active shares.
Revoke a share by its id.
Cached global aggregates (active/archived counts + per-payload totals).

groups.title: Sessions & Console
groups.note: Access inherits the session's payload: viewing needs view access, enqueueing commands needs edit access. A session is a (client_id + origin) group keyed by its representative row id.

rows.params: query: page, per_page, search, payload, archive
rows.d: Paginated grouped listing, scoped by payload access (admins: all). payload=__catchall__ (admin) lists session groups coupled to no payload. Pagination in meta.
One session group with the decompressed blob.
The group's request/navigation history.
One request row (full).
Toggle the group's archive flag.
Delete the group plus its data and console rows.

rows.params: query: archive, payload, search, seen_within, seen_before
rows.d: Number of groups the given filter resolves to (the bulk blast-radius). Scoped to the caller's payloads.
Distinct payload identifiers that actually have sessions, for the filter dropdown (scoped for non-admins).
Archive/unarchive/delete many groups at once, by id list or by a scope filter. Capped per request.
Enqueue a raw-JS console command for the session group (201). Evaluated by the persistent client on its next ping.
List queued + already-sent commands for the group.
The group's aggregated console output.
Start the reverse proxy (ezProxy) on the session.
Enqueue ez_stop() to stop the persistent client.
Drop the client's auto-reconnect flag.
Enqueue a console command (or archive/delete action) to many session groups in one request (201).

groups.title: Alerts
groups.note: Own destinations are per-user; the global rows + method master switches are admin-only (settings.manage). An alert fires only when BOTH the method switch and the row are enabled.

rows.d: The current user's own alert destinations (mail / telegram / slack / discord) + per-row enable.
Update the current user's own destinations.
Global destinations + the alert-method master switches + callback-url.
Update the global destinations and master switches.
Send a test alert to the caller's own destinations.
Resolve a Telegram bot token to its chat id, to help set up the Telegram destination.

groups.title: Extensions
groups.note: Payload extensions are global/admin-managed - every action requires settings.manage.

rows.d: List extensions (metadata only, no code).
Create an extension (201).
One extension including its code.
Update an extension's editable fields.
Delete an extension.
Toggle the enabled flag; returns the new state.
Install extension(s) from a remote source URL (201).
GET checks the extension's remote source for a newer version; POST applies the update.

groups.title: Settings
groups.note: Application/payload/global settings (NOT the alert destinations - those are owned by /api/alerts). Every write requires settings.manage; updates are partial.

rows.d: Read all owned settings plus an 'available' block of selectable options.
Validate and persist only the fields present in the body.
Arm the platform kill switch. While armed every request 404s until any URL is visited with ?pass=<password>.

groups.title: Dashboard & Logs
groups.note: The dashboard needs report.view and scopes to the caller; the audit log is admin-only global data.

rows.d: The dashboard stat tiles (admins read the cached global aggregate; others get a scoped live aggregate).
Top-10 most-common {value,count} for one field.
Current vs latest ezXSS version (cached) for the update card.
Paginated audit log (newest first). Pagination in meta.

groups.title: System & lifecycle
groups.note: Status/install/update stay reachable before the instance is installed so the first-run screens can drive setup.

rows.d: Liveness probe. Returns "pong".
Coarse instance state { state: db_error|not_installed|upgrade|ready, version }. Leaks nothing sensitive.
{ installed: bool } so the first-run UI can detect install state.
One-time installer: run migrations, seed settings, create the first admin (201). Refuses once installed (409).
{ current_version, code_version, legacy, pending[], needs_update } - version strings + migration filenames only.

Apply pending migrations and bump the stored version. Runs WITHOUT a bearer - updating the panel is a system-wide action, not a per-user permission - and is rate-limited per IP; advises enabling IP_LOCK.

groups.title: Public surface (outside /api)
groups.note: No auth, open CORS. These are the live collector + panel paths the payload and browser use.

rows.d: Serve the assembled payload JavaScript. A request serves the payload coupled to its host/path, or the catch-all (built from the instance's default settings) when none matches; /{name} serves a named custom payload. Also reachable at /api/payload.
Report-ingest endpoint the served payload POSTs to. Always answers the plain placeholder body; never leaks internals. Also at /api/callback.
Deferred heavy-field ingest (dom, screenshot). The main callback returns an attach token; the payload sends large fields here in a follow-up request.

rows.params: path: slug (25 lowercase chars); append .json for the data feed
rows.d: Public view of an on-request report share - a readable HTML page, with /s/{slug}.json serving the same selected columns as JSON. Expiry respected (410 when expired).
CSP-bypass beacon sinks. Always return a strictly-typed empty resource for the type and record the inferred-CSP signal.
The admin panel SPA shell. The same static HTML answers /manage and every client-router deep link; all its data calls go through the authenticated /api surface.
